Mr. Speaker, Sir, I beg to reply and urge Senators to support this Motion so that we uphold the discipline in Jubilee Party and other political parties, generally. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I received the notification.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: On a point of order. Mr. Speaker, Sir. On what basis does someone vote on behalf of someone else?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Let us vote. I will give direction on that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, on what constitutional basis can one--- The Constitution is very clear.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: The former Senate Majority Leader, remember I made a ruling here that in such exceptional times--- Even when you were the Senate Majority Leader, we were also taking votes through proxy. She has written and she is indisposed. It was brought---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, there can be no worse violation of our Constitution than that. There is no one---. There was never a time we sat in the Senate Business Committee to approve a Member who is not in the Senate Chamber to vote. It is impossible. Mr. Speaker, Sir, in fact, it is the greatest violation of our Constitution. Please, do not go there. You already have the numbers to remove the Deputy Speaker. Do not rape our Constitution further.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, at least, if you give somebody latitude---. The words that are being used on the Floor of the House like 'rape,' what would young people, and particularly our women, think about our language? I think we should use language with decorum.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I insist that allowing a person who is not in the Chamber and not within the vicinity of Parliament to vote, is not only rape. I would rather use 'defilement' because it is worse.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Sen. Murkomen, Sen. Mugo was here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, even if she was here.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: An hon. Senator
entries.text: Yes!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Susan Wakarura Kihika
entries.text: Who are you shouting at?

entries.label: scene

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Sen. Murkomen! She was here and because of illness, which was brought to my attention, that is how I allowed it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is impossible. It is not for you, Mr. Speaker, Sir, to allow. It is impossible and unconstitutional. There is absolutely no basis for you to defile this Constitution. You have the numbers. Do not go there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ochilo George Mbogo Ayacko
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this is a House of order. If you allow Members to talk back, overrule and heckle you, I am the best at that. Do not allow this because when others start it, this House will be disorderly. So, make your ruling with finality. I beg you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Sen. Olekina, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would not want to slow down the process. However, because we are talking about procedures, Standing Order No.1 gives the Speaker latitude to make certain decisions. I do not know whether this would apply to the issue of a Senator voting on behalf of another.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Order, Members! Let the voting continue. I will make a ruling at the end of it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: Yes!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: Let us proceed.

entries.label: speech

entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, yes, I have his letter. He says he votes "Yes". But I agree, we can keep it aside, pending your ruling.

entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have a point of order.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: What is your point of order?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Irungu Kang'ata
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I propose we exclude the two contentious votes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.text: I was going to make a ruling on that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Irungu Kang'ata
entries.text: Exclude the votes for abundance of caution.
